Data centre.d: A large building full of servers, networking, power supplies and cooling. AI models are trained and served from data centres, not from your own computer.

TPU.d: Tensor processing unit: an AI accelerator chip designed by Google for neural-network maths, used for Gemini and rented out through Google Cloud.

Memory bandwidth.d: How fast a chip can move data from its memory to its calculating units. For generating text token by token, it is often the main limit on speed.

KV cache.d: Stored intermediate results (attention keys and values) for the tokens a model has already processed, kept in chip memory so they don't have to be recalculated for every new token. It grows with conversation length.

Prompt caching.d: Reusing the already-processed form of a repeated prompt prefix (such as long instructions or a document) across requests. Cached input is charged at a small fraction of the normal price.

Latency.d: How long one user waits for a response. For AI, often measured as time to first token plus how fast the rest of the reply streams.

Time to first token.d: How long after sending a request the first piece of the model's reply appears. It is what people feel most as 'waiting' in a chat.

Throughput.d: How much total work a system gets through, such as tokens or requests per second across all users. Batching raises throughput, sometimes at the cost of latency.

Foundation model.d: A large, general-purpose model trained on broad data that many different products and tasks can be built on, such as GPT, Claude, Gemini or Llama.

Hyperscaler.d: A cloud provider operating at enormous scale, chiefly Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. All three also sell access to AI models.

Public benefit corporation.d: A for-profit company legally required to weigh a stated public benefit alongside shareholders' interests. Both Anthropic and OpenAI's operating company are public benefit corporations.
